title: GTA 6 On Switch 2? Digital Foundry Weighs In On The Possibility
summary:
A pipe dream port?

Could Grand Theft Auto 6 come to Switch 2? That has been the big question ever since Nintendo officially revealed its console last year, and it's something that we have mused over ever since (as unlikely as it may seem at an initial glance). Now that the game is out, the tech experts over at Digital Foundry have weighed in on the port possibility, and, perhaps unsurprisingly, they don't rate its chances.

In the outlet's latest rundown, it touches on the "compromised" Xbox Series S performance. It isn't all that, with DF noting "frame-rates routinely lingering in the mid to high 20s during ordinary traversal and combat," but it's the system that regularly lands the most comparisons to Switch 2, so DF says that it would be "interesting" to see if it would be "possible for a further cut back version to ship on Nintendo's hybrid console".

summary:
Oli-marred.

The latest Japanese charts data is in, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has comfortably maintained its lead with another 86,097 sales. Next in line is Metaphor: ReFantazio as its hits the Switch 2, shifting a total of 11,167 units.

Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy also made its debut, selling just 2,854 copies to land at number 9. Now, it's important to note that many owners of the game on Switch 1 will have simply bought the upgrade pack, which won't count toward this total, however the game has also seen its fair share of controversy soon after release.

title: 8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2
summary:
And it's more affordable than Nintendo's.

8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has announced the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary. It's currently scheduled to launch on 10th December 2026.

Compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers. Priced at $49.99, it undercuts Nintendo's official offering by $20 and is available for pre-order now.
